summary: R6: queue add --continue writes --queued --requested (starts even after a stop); --automatic (finish() after a session cap, the debrief) omits it and is skipped after a stop; queue list marks (requested)/(automatic), parked too. A request upgrades a queued automatic entry; a stop the driver honours demotes its run's queued requests. R11: numbers past held/, park refuses to overwrite.
verified_how: check.sh: green in 637 s, 341/341 (was 333). 8 new checks written first and watched failing (6/6 then 2/2 red on a scratch subset), then green; the adapted stoppy/stoppy-o setups and the debrief continuation check pass. bash -n on bin/harness, lib/driver.sh, lib/debrief.sh, tests/run.sh.

dead_ends.tried: asserting ndb == 1 in the requested-continuation check
dead_ends.why: only true in the full suite's order; made it relative (B=$(ndb))

discoveries.text: An Opus review found that a request queued while a run is still going would undo a later stop. Fix: demote_requests() in lib/driver.sh runs just before the stop site (`[[ $c == stop ]] && demote_requests`, on its own line). F1-05 (R7) edits the next line: keep the call.

Drivers started before this merge still call queue add --continue without --automatic at a session cap, so their continuations read (requested) until those drivers exit; entries queued before it list as (automatic).

The real-systemd scope check (scope.sh: a real 64M scope kills a 256 MB allocation) failed once in a full run while another agent was busy, then passed alone and in the next full run: flaky under load.

questions: D *default*: a stop after a requested continuation wins. The driver turns that request automatic, so the run doesn't restart. A request made after the stop still starts it. Keep it that way, or should a request always start the run whatever comes after it?
